groups.canonical_citation: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (DND, Feb. 2017)
groups.conflict_note: This is a city administrative policy applicable only to DND-funded or income-restricted housing providers, not all Boston landlords; it operates alongside (and may be narrower than) general state and federal fair-housing/CORI law.
groups.interaction: Overlaps with M.G.L. c.151B's general anti-discrimination protections; this policy adds specific criminal-history lookback and credit-score restrictions for city-funded housing only.

groups.canonical_citation: Boston Fair Housing Regulations - Source of Income Protection
groups.interaction: Overlaps with the statewide prohibition on discrimination based on public assistance/housing subsidies (M.G.L. c.151B, §4(10)); Boston's rule explicitly names Section 8, disability, and veterans vouchers.

groups.canonical_citation: Boston Mun. Code, Housing Stability Notification Act, Sec. 10-11.7
groups.interaction: Supplements state notice-to-quit requirements (M.G.L. c.186, §11/§12) with an additional city notice and reporting obligation.
Overlaps with the statewide source-of-income/public-assistance discrimination prohibition under M.G.L. c.151B, §4(10).
Imposes a stricter per-fee cap ($25) for buildings with six or more units than the general statewide limitation on pre-tenancy charges under M.G.L. c.186, §15B.

groups.canonical_citation: Mass. Initiative Petition 25-21 (2026); Cella v. Attorney General, SJC-13893
groups.conflict_note: Petition was blocked by the SJC from the November 2026 ballot due to an unconstitutional religious-facility exemption; had it passed it would have repealed the statewide rent-control ban (M.G.L. c.40P).
groups.interaction: Would have superseded the statewide prohibition on rent control (M.G.L. c.40P) by authorizing a capped rent-increase scheme statewide, but never took effect.
Local ordinances such as Boston's and Cambridge's source-of-income protections overlap with and reinforce this statewide prohibition.
